note: Written by hand from the runs of tools/role_walk.py (walk.json beside this file). basis: shown = a test or run of this card showed it (the test is named); hypothesis = read from code, not run; not_run = not run. ruling: a decision that records the behaviour. Places are on master 7da6edd3.
verdict: Against a committed table of what each console route must ask (tests/console/data/route_actions.yaml), no console route let a column in that its row refuses; the walk decided 3,895 of 4,424 console cells and all 968 orchestrator cells, and 529 console cells stay unclear (the check was not seen to be reached; pinned by route and column). Refused against the row: three cells where the EDC router refuses the study's PI (V2-05) and four orchestrator cells ruled by D-871 and D-864 (V2-01). The set-up page shows a raw text key on a refused SAE rule set (V2-06). The two-person rules and break-glass hold, also for one person who switches roles. Not walked: the compose box, and the orchestrator's v2 groups beyond V2-05's cells. 236 of the table's 316 rows were drafted from a traced walk and not checked against a decision by hand.

findings.claim: Ruled by D-871 and D-864; the matrix has no row that says it: the job cancel (declares request.prepare, also asks ops.view) and an instrument switch (declares site.setup, then role == admin) refuse a coordinator the declared row allows.
findings.expected: each role may do exactly what the matrix says (plan 8 V8, criterion 10); D-871 and D-864 chose not to add a row (the guides are frozen)
findings.happened: 403 reason right for the coordinator on POST /jobs/{job_id}/cancel and PUT /setup/instruments/{iid}

findings.claim: 46 refusals on 9 console routes write no audit record (2,554 of the 2,603 refusals with 403 to a signed-in column are recorded; the other 3 are V2-05's, recorded by the orchestrator); among them the administrator's, the steward's and the privacy office's refused attempt to open a patient page.
findings.expected: No decision asks for a refusal record on these routes; decisions ask it per page elsewhere (D-207 /ops/flags, D-443 /data-ops, D-451 /audit, D-436 the monitor pages) and D-483 2. for every orchestrator call. Judged against 'an audit trail that can be wrong' (High): the trail holds nothing false, but an attempted patient access leaves no trace where the same page records its delegation refusal (home.py screen_or_403), so Medium (the record is incomplete, not wrong)
findings.happened: 403 and no audit record written by the request (counted per request by its tag; walk.json cells with got R, status 403, audited 0)

findings.claim: The orchestrator compares a role name in two places with no matrix row behind them: the blind re-entry record (a.role != "admin", edc_api.py:260) and the instrument switch (who.role != "admin", setup_api.py:84); the grep test against inline role checks reads console modules only (test_t102c_permit_sites.py:59).
findings.expected: one permission function over the matrix, no inline role check (D-366, D-425)
findings.happened: both lines read on master 15108f46 as cited; the matrix has no row for either action, so the role pages generated from it (ROLE-018) do not name them
findings.test: read from code; the coordinator's refusal on the re-entry route runs in tests/console/test_matrix_role_walk_rules.py::test_two_person_edc_reentry_and_switch_on

findings.claim: The committed role x route design table says the steward and the privacy office open a study's candidate registry page (patient rows); the box refuses them only because the backend signs the read: the page has no check of its own, and the test box's stand-in backend skips that layer.
findings.place: tests/console/data/role_route_matrix.md:107; tests/console/test_console_app.py:307 (FakeBackend.registry_rows); services/console/app.py:2246 (the page); services/console/backend.py:539 (the signed read)
findings.expected: the design table equals what the box answers (D-366 5.); the registry's rows are patient level (app.py:2253, D-280)
findings.happened: with the stand-in as it is, GET /pilot/registry/GZQO answers 200 to the steward and the privacy office; with the signing layer put back (test_matrix_role_walk.faithful_reads) it answers 403, as the declared row [phi.view, task.screen] says

findings.claim: The orchestrator's EDC router refuses the study's PI the copy sheet, the ODM export and the send (edc.role), which the matrix gives an investigator holding enter_data and the log's PI holds every task: edc_role_may reads the investigator as on no log, and since D-380 such an investigator holds no task.
findings.expected: the matrix's edc.copy, edc.export, edc.send: investigator [task:enter_data] (D-160, D-434); the PI holds every task (D-380)
findings.happened: 403 edc.role for the PI on GET /api/v1/studies/{rs}/edc/copy, /edc/export/odm and POST /edc/send in the walk; the router alone refuses GET /studies/{rs}/edc/copy and /edc/export/odm to an investigator

findings.claim: The study set-up page names a refused SAE rule set through t('rc.err.' + code); the orchestrator's code LIFE-STEP has no catalogue entry, so a box shows the raw key rc.err.LIFE-STEP to the coordinator, and the tests' strict text mode (D-1220) turns the page into a 500.
findings.expected: D-1220: a text key the page asks for has a catalogue entry; a page never shows a raw key
findings.happened: POST /studies/{rs}/setup/sae with no rule set, as a coordinator: MissingText 'rc.err.LIFE-STEP' in strict mode (a 500 in the walk, the cells crc and smo_in pinned unclear with this reason); on a box the key is shown as written
